newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Tajikistan talks to resume in Iran on Monday - U.N.
newsitem.headline: Tajikistan talks to resume in Iran on Monday - U.N.

text.p: Tajikistan government officials and opposition leaders will resume talks on power sharing in the turbulent central Asian country, on Monday in Tehran, the United Nations said on Friday.
The two sides signed an accord in Moscow on Dec. 23 and set a July 1 deadline to put it into force, after which a 12- to 18-month transition period would follow.

The agreement called for an immediate ceasefire, an amnesty, an exchange of war prisoners and the creation of a Commission on National Reconciliation with powers to change the composition of the government and hold parliamentary elections or call a referendum on the constitution.

Spokesman Fred Eckhard said the composition of the commission was expected to be one of the main issues under discussion in the Iranian capital next week. Gerd Merrem of Germany, the U.N. special representative, will be at the talks.

After years of broken cease-fires, Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri last month signed the agreement, saying that their country of nearly 6 million people had suffered enough.
Tens of thousand of people have been killed in a four-year civil war between Tajikistan's secular government and Islamist guerrillas, spawned by the collapse of the Soviet Union.
A 96-member U.N. Mission of Observers in Tajikistan (UNMOT) works with a much larger peacekeeping force fielded by Russia and the Commonwealth of Independent States.
The rebels control the mountainous eastern half of Tajikistan, which houses about 10 percent of the population.
